/-!
# Erdős Problem 435

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/435](https://www.erdosproblems.com/435)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [HwSo24] W. Hwang and K. Song, *The Frobenius problem for Numerical Semigroups generated by
  binomial coefficients*. arXiv:2412.17882 (2024).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos435

/--
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\neq p^k$ for any prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. What is the largest
integer not of the form
$$\sum_{1\leq i<n}c_i\binom{n}{i}$$
where the $c_i\geq 0$ are integers?

If $n=\prod p_k^{a_k}$ then the largest integer not of this form is
$$\sum_k \left( \sum_{1\leq d\leq a_k}\binom{n}{p_k^d}\right)(p_k-1)-n.$$
This was first proved by Hwang and Song [HwSo24]. Independently this was found in the comment
section by Peake and Cambie.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos435.lean"]
theorem erdos_435 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hpk : ∀ p k : ℕ, p.Prime → n ≠ p ^ k) :
    IsGreatest
      {m : ℤ | ¬ ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, m = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n, (c i : ℤ) * (n.choose i : ℤ)}
      ((∑ p ∈ n.primeFactors,
        (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n.factorization p), (n.choose (p ^ d) : ℤ)) * ((p : ℤ) - 1)) - n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos435

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos435.erdos_435, faithfully states the explicit solution. The natural-valued coefficients are precisely nonnegative integer coefficients; Ico 1 n gives 1 ≤ i < n; primeFactors and factorization give distinct prime divisors and their multiplicities. Both subtractions occur in ℤ. The hypotheses exclude 0, 1, and all prime powers and force n ≥ 6; their satisfiability at n = 6 was proved in scratch Lean. An independent residue-class computation matched the formula for every admissible n ≤ 100. Scratch proofs also established equivalence with the linked proof's additive-submonoid formulation, using only standard axioms. The research solved category agrees with Hwang–Song. Access to erdosproblems.com/435 and its forum was blocked by Cloudflare, so the mathematical comparison used the original book and the cited paper. The linked proof contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms, but its declared Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 environment was unavailable; recompilation under 4.33.1 encountered compatibility errors. This is a verification limitation, not evidence of an incorrect proof-status record. The reviewed file was not modified.
